subject: Zenvera post-demo: retention, audit logs & PII handling — next steps
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
To: Ethan Cole <ethan@zenvera.com>
Cc: Olivia Park <olivia@zenvera.com>, Olga Petrov <olga@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 05 Dec 2026 15:12:00 -0800
Subject: Zenvera post-demo: retention, audit logs & PII handling — next steps

Hi Ethan / Olivia — thanks again for the demo time today. Quick recap while it's fresh and to make sure we're aligned on scope for a short POC: 

Summary of pain points you shared:
- Legal requires long-term auditability for a subset of records (potentially up to 7 years) but product team wants short retention for transient logs to reduce risk.
- Current pipeline sends verbose request traces to Splunk; sensitive fields occasionally appear in free-text metadata.
- Need the ability to produce an auditable redaction artifact (proof that PII was detected and redacted) for compliance requests.

Current stack you mentioned:
- GCP Pub/Sub --> BigQuery for analytics, Splunk for logs.
- Customer-facing inference runs in GKE; model outputs are stored in S3-compatible buckets for downstream tooling.

Success criteria for a successful POC (your notes + our interpretation):
1) PII not present in Redwood-hosted logs for production traffic (we should confirm exact columns/fields you consider PII).
2) Audit log export for requests touching regulated data (readable, tamper-evident) for N days/months — and an option to archive extracts for 7 years for regulated datasets.
3) Observed 90th pct latency under 250ms for typical inference (60–512 token ranges) during the POC window.
4) Integration with your SSO and ability to demonstrate role-based access to audit logs.

Proposed next steps I recommend: 
- You: share a small sample of sanitized logs (we discussed < 500 requests) and a redaction whitelist/blacklist that your legal must retain for audit. (Attachment: "zenvera-sample-logs-PII-sanitized.json")
- Us: deliver a short scope doc (attached: "initial_scope_template.docx") that maps retention profiles and redaction outputs to the above success criteria.
- Security: Olga will run the SOC2 mapping + quick answers; we can also surface the cryptographic signing approach we use for tamper evidence.
- Schedule: propose a 60-minute technical POC on Dec 15 or Dec 17 — which works for you?

Attachments: Zenvera_demo_recording.mp4 (recording link included in HubSpot), initial_scope_template.docx.

If this looks right I can draft the POC schedule and invite the right product/infra folks.

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0198

--
Redwood Inference — Make inference predictable and economical
From: Ethan Cole <ethan@zenvera.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
Cc: Olivia Park <olivia@zenvera.com>
Date: Sat, 06 Dec 2026 09:04:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Zenvera post-demo: retention, audit logs & PII handling — next steps

Marissa — appreciate the summary and clear checklist. A few clarifications from our side: 

- Retention: Legal's baseline for PHI-adjacent artifacts is 7 years for specific cohorts (billing/claims), but for transient inference logs product would prefer 3 years. For the POC we can focus on two profiles: "transient" = 3 years, "regulated" = 7 years.
- Redaction: We currently use tokenization/hashing for direct identifiers and strict regex redaction for patterns (SSNs, card numbers). Can Redwood provide either hashing or irreversible tokenization for PII in logs? We need an evidence artifact that shows which tokens were redacted and by which rule.
- Stack nuance: while analytics live in BigQuery, our live observability pipeline still ships raw traces into Splunk. We want to validate that Redwood's KV cache & prefix caching won't leak sensitive substrings into logs (this is a vendor concern).

I attached a sanitized sample logs file for the POC. We'll also need a short security questionnaire answered by next Wed so our infosec can triage.

Dates: Dec 15 works for a 9am PT slot. I'll confirm with Olivia.

Ethan
Director, Platform Eng — Zenvera Health
ethan@zenvera.com

Subject: Re: Zenvera post-demo: retention, audit logs & PII handling — next steps

Marissa — quick internal note on approach.

A few tactical suggestions before we commit the POC scope: 
1) Offer two retention profiles as Ethan suggested and map them to Redwood's archiving/export flow — don't propose '7 years in prod' as default; present archive-to-cold-storage option (signed manifests + S3 Glacier replacement).
2) For redaction evidence: provide both (a) an export of the redaction log (timestamp, rule-id, hashed-value) and (b) a signed manifest that shows the pre/post check-sum for each exported bundle. That aligns well with audit requests.
3) Ask Olga to prepare a short SOC2 / collection map (questions we can answer within 48 hours) and surface any gaps.

I'll loop in Legal if they ask for contract language around retention/escrow. If you want, I can join the Dec 15 POC for the compliance section.

-Karthik
VP, Sales Engineering

Marissa / Olga — thanks, both. Confirming: 

- We will go ahead with the POC. I uploaded the sanitized log sample to the shared Drive link you included.
- Dec 15 at 9am PT is good for the POC. Please send calendar invite.
- Infosec will send a short questionnaire (I expect by Monday) — Olga, if you can prefill what you can that will help us move faster.
- We prefer irreversible tokenization for PII in logs if Redwood supports that; otherwise hashing with peppering is acceptable if you can provide proof artifacts.

DocuSign: I'll have our legal team review the NDA link you provided. Happy to sign once we get the scope doc.

Thanks — looking forward to the POC.

Ethan
